title: Early stage of my AI game journey
author: sheeburashka
selftext:
Hey all,

For the past three months I've been building a game called Qaldera on evenings and weekends. It's a dark-fantasy ARPG in the spirit of Diablo 2, and you can play it in your browser or on your phone.

Some background, because the how is half the fun of this project. I'm not a programmer. This started as a way to see what new AI models could do outside of work, and it kept growing. I began with Claude Opus 5.0, moved to Fable, and now it's mostly Opus 5.5 running things.

At this point Opus 5.5 handles the orchestration end to end. It writes the code, sends image requests to OpenAI's Codex image tool for concept art and icons, and queues up 3D model jobs in ComfyUI that run locally on my 5070 Ti. We also built a little orchestration tool that keeps a queue of jobs going overnight so the PC isn't sitting idle. It balances GPU and CPU load and paces everything around my weekly usage limits, so I wake up to a batch of new models and fixes to look at.

A couple of things that made a big difference, in case you're trying something similar:

* Keep a written "lessons learned" file and bug log that every session reads first. Before I did that, it kept re-breaking things it had already fixed.
* Have it build automated checks for the stuff you care about. Mine plays a session in a headless browser and fails if the game freezes mid-fight, since that was my worst bug for a while.

I also deliberately avoided Higgsfield and the other easy 3D asset generators. I wanted to see if I could get a polished look without yet another subscription. I'll admit 3D has been the toughest part, and I haven't gotten it where I want it yet. The initial renders look great, but the look doesn't carry through into the game very well. If anyone has advice on that, I'd really appreciate it.

**What's in it so far**

* 8 classes with 160 skills between them
* 132 named legendaries, crafting at the Mirror Forge, and a merchant you can gamble with
* A "two worlds" mechanic where you flip between two versions of reality mid-fight
* A story in four acts with dungeons and bosses
* A town, an overworld you can ride and fly across, and an iso or over-the-shoulder camera (V to switch)

It's still early and there's plenty to improve, so I'm sure you'll find rough spots. I'm having a lot of fun building it, though.

**Check it out here:** [**https://qaldera.xyz**](https://qaldera.xyz/)

Thanks for reading, and thanks to anyone who gives it a try. I'll be in the comments.
